You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2016. The fed funds rate is 0.40% and the unemployment rate is 4.9%. The 10-year yield is 1.57% after falling 0.27 over three months, so rates were still low but had risen from the summer. Core CPI is 2.16% and headline CPI is 0.88%, both consistent with 2016.

The 10-year at 1.57% points to a month between July and September 2016, when it was roughly 1.5% to 1.6%. The 12-month change in the dollar of -16 pp looks odd, but the YoY level of +0.66% fits mid-2016. The fed funds rate was about 0.40% in both August and September 2016, though the 3m change of +0.11 means it was rising. The rate was 0.29% in May and 0.40% in August, so the 3m change fits August. The 10-year was about 1.56% in August 2016.

The 10-year was 1.83% in May, which gives a 3m change of -0.27 for August. Gold fell 4.2% in the month, but gold was roughly flat in August 2016 and fell in September, so the gold figure is less clear. The VIX at 13.12 fits August, when it was about 11 to 13. The 12m change of -15.31 follows from the August 2015 spike to about 28. Headline CPI in July 2016 was 0.84% and the unemployment rate was 4.9%, so August fits.

The gold 1m return of -4.2% is hard to square with August, though. If it were measured through the end of August, gold would be about -0.5%. It is possible the snapshot is for September, when gold fell about 4% from its August level, but the 10-year would then be about 1.60% and the 3m change would be smaller. The fed funds rate was 0.40% in both months. Equities at +0.8% over 1m fits September better, since the S&P was flat that month. Developed ex-US equity at +1.7% and EM at +1.8% also fit September, as does the 3m EM return of +10.3%. Core CPI at 2.16% fits August data, published in September. I'll go with September.

```json
{"year":2016,"month":9,"confidence":0.6,"cues":["Fed funds 0.40% and unemployment 4.9%","10-year yield 1.57% with a -0.27 3m change","Gold -4.2% in the month with equities only +0.8%"]}
```
